meta.eyebrow: DEMO-7 · Reporting service in a test account · engineer's view
meta.title: The test account by Friday is buildable, but three open choices decide its shape: storage, access and size
meta.lede: The ticket asks for two servers. The diagram attached to it also needs a load balancer and a certificate. The reference copy is bigger and older than either. Until three things are settled we cannot approve a plan. Ticket [r2].
meta.foot: Source: a made-up scenario for testing the readout template. Colours are the author's reading, not a measurement.

nodes.title: 2 servers, medium size, test account by Friday
nodes.plain: The ticket lists one app server and one database server, both medium. Production follows next month.
nodes.needs: Confirm sizing and what done includes.

nodes.title: Also an ALB and a certificate
nodes.plain: The diagram in a comment needs HTTPS in front of the app. Those pieces are not in the ticket list.
nodes.needs: Is the front door in scope for the test account?

nodes.title: demo-reference: 3 servers, 2 SG, ALB
nodes.plain: The reference folder already builds the full pattern and is proven. It uses large servers and keeps database backups with PITR.

nodes.title: Server library 1.3, eight majors behind
nodes.plain: The reference pins old library versions. Copying them works but is old.
nodes.needs: Which source is the truth for versions?

nodes.title: Test account is empty; name unknown
nodes.plain: The test folder is an empty scaffold. The ticket carries no account code, so the name cannot be derived.

nodes.title: Draft branch reported, not visible
nodes.plain: A comment mentions a draft branch, but the branch list shows none. It may be unpushed.
nodes.needs: Ask the owner before duplicating work.

nodes.title: Handoff table lists servers only
nodes.plain: After apply, the handoff table may show servers only and miss the ALB.
nodes.needs: Test with a state holding every resource type.

problem: We are asked to copy a proven pattern into an empty account on a deadline, but the ticket, the diagram and the pattern describe three different systems [r1], and we do not yet know the account name or whether someone has started a branch.

choices.question: how to store and back up data
choices.why: Decide once we know which library source is the truth.

options.title: Copy the reference storage
options.con: Old; becomes debt on day one

options.title: Copy now, upgrade in a follow-up
options.pro: Meets the date and keeps the upgrade visible

choices.question: what is in scope for the test account
choices.why: Decide once the requester confirms whether HTTPS is needed on day one.

options.title: Servers plus ALB and certificate
options.con: Needs a DNS name, not yet known

options.title: Servers first, front door second
options.pro: Unblocks servers while DNS is settled
options.con: Test account not fully usable at first

choices.question: what size the servers are
choices.why: Decide once the requester confirms the ticket sizing.

options.title: Medium for both, as the ticket says
Medium now, resize if tests show a need
options.pro: Follows the ticket and stays reversible
options.con: Needs a resize step in the runbook

needs.need: The DNS name and certificate domain
Confirmation that the front door is in scope
Confirmation of sizing: ticket says medium, reference uses large

needs.settles: Whether the change can be drafted at all

needs.need: Which registry holds the true library versions

risks.risk: Sizing is half the reference; the database may be undersized
risks.action: Start at the ticket size and add a resize step to the runbook.

risks.risk: We duplicate work already on an unpushed branch
risks.action: Ask the owner before opening anything.

risks.risk: Copied pins are eight majors old
risks.action: Record the choice and open the upgrade as its own task.

risks.risk: Test and production arrive in one ticket
risks.action: One environment per change; production waits until next month.

refs.title: Doc system principles: say which kind of claim it is

glossary.ALB: a load balancer: the front door that spreads web traffic across servers
glossary.SG: security group: the firewall rules around a server
glossary.PITR: point-in-time recovery: restore a database to any moment in the last days
